reason: I'll start with the bearing frames to support the rotating shaft on the base.
expectation: The frames will fit onto the base, ready to hold the crankshaft.

alternatives.reason: The follower and guide also seem useful, but supporting the shaft feels like a good starting point.

effect: The base now has bearings to support the shaft, so I can fit the crankshaft next.
reaction: That was a straightforward first assembly step.
reason: The crankshaft should fit into the bearings and provide the rotating part of the mechanism.
expectation: I expect the shaft to sit in the bearing frames, ready for other parts.

alternatives.reason: The follower assembly is also needed, but I want to finish supporting the shaft first.

effect: The crankshaft now turns in the frame, ready for the cam.
reaction: The shaft assembly is coming together straightforwardly.
reason: The off-centre cam should turn with the shaft and help lift the follower.
expectation: I expect the cam to attach to the crankshaft, though the follower will still need fitting.

alternatives.reason: The follower and guide also need assembling, but I want to add the cam first.

effect: The cam's changing edge height explains how rotation can lift the follower; a centred disc would not do that.
reaction: The contrast with a centred disc makes the mechanism satisfyingly clear.
reason: The follower rod and guide are the only offered combination, and the guide should keep the rod aligned.
expectation: I expect an assembled follower that can later be fitted above the cam.

effect: The follower is assembled in its guide and can now be fitted to the cam mechanism.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should position the follower against the cam.
expectation: I expect the guided rod to attach above the cam so it can rise and fall as the shaft turns.

effect: The guided follower is now positioned above the cam, so the mechanism is ready for a way to turn it.
reaction: The parts are coming together as expected.
reason: The crank handle is the only offered combination and should let me turn the shaft.
expectation: I expect the handle to attach so I can turn the cam and see whether the follower moves.

effect: The test shows the rod can stick instead of following the cam downward, so it needs help maintaining contact.
reaction: The unexpected snag makes the spring's purpose clearer.
reason: The spring is the only offered combination and should help keep the follower against the cam.
expectation: I expect the spring to press the follower toward the cam so the rod rises and falls reliably.

effect: The spring keeps the follower in contact with the cam, completing the reliable up-and-down motion.
reaction: Seeing the earlier sticking problem resolved was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the off-centre cam was most worthwhile: comparing it with a centred disc clearly explained how rotation becomes a change in height.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the follower into its guide was straightforward but less informative on its own.

surprise.text: The follower sometimes stuck in its guide and lost contact with the cam; that made the spring's role clear.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; even the simple assembly steps had a clear role in the mechanism.

continue.text: Yes. The working cam was interesting to understand, and I would like to see how it makes the paper dragon wave.
